title: Source tax tariff: denomination, spouse employment and tariff code
purpose: Ask employees subject to source tax for their denomination and, if married or in a registered partnership, whether the spouse or partner works. Combine these with the child digit and the cross-border result into the computed Zurich tariff code that Lonio records for HR.

stories.title: Ask the religious denomination only where source tax needs it and derive the church-tax suffix
stories.i_want: to be asked for my religious denomination only if I am subject to source tax
stories.so_that: Lonio can set the church-tax suffix of my source tax tariff code without collecting my religion when no receiving party needs it
stories.priority_reason: Every tariff code ends in the church-tax suffix. Without it Lonio cannot compute the code (D-001), and HR would be back to clicking through the calculator by hand (F-hr_transcript-3cd6fa). Asking it of everyone would break data minimisation (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination is asked only of employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee whose earlier answers make them subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax: living abroad, or living in Switzerland without Swiss citizenship, without a C permit and without the spouse exemption)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the denomination question is asked and must be answered. Employees not subject to source tax are never asked it. The income type is not asked first, because a new employee always has earned income (D-006).

examples.name: Swiss citizen living abroad, like Stefan (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)
Non-Swiss employee in Switzerland without C permit

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination offers exactly the calculator's two choices
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee chooses exactly one of 'Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed' or 'None or other'. No other denomination is offered or recorded, and the answer is recorded for HR for the source tax tariff.

acceptance_criteria.title: Church-tax suffix follows the denomination
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax who has answered the denomination question
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the church-tax suffix of the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.then: the suffix is Y for 'Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed' and N for 'None or other'. It is derived again whenever the denomination answer changes (D-037).

given.value: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

stories.title: Ask married employees and registered partners subject to source tax whether their spouse or partner works
stories.i_want: to be asked whether my spouse or registered partner works only if I am subject to source tax and married or in a registered partnership
stories.so_that: Lonio can choose between tariff C and B for me without asking anyone else about their partner
stories.priority_reason: HR names this as the question that changes the calculator's result for married employees (F-hr_transcript-6a0a40). Without it the tariff code cannot be computed (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse employment is asked only of married employees and registered partners subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee whose civil status and source tax liability (rule subject_to_source_tax) are known
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the question 'Does your spouse or registered partner work or receive replacement income?' is asked and must be answered only if the employee is subject to source tax and their civil status is Married or Registered partnership. It is not asked of Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated employees, because for source tax separated counts as single (D-003). It is not asked of anyone who is not subject to source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse employment is a yes/no answer recorded for source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse employment question is asked
acceptance_criteria.then: the answer is 'yes' (the spouse or partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income) or 'no'. It is recorded for HR as the input that decides between tariff letter C and B.

stories.title: Derive the base source tax tariff letter
stories.i_want: the base tariff letter (A, B, C or H) of every employee subject to source tax to be derived from civil status, spouse employment and the children, as the Zurich calculator does
stories.so_that: the employee is taxed at the right base tariff without HR deciding the letter by hand
stories.priority_reason: Today HR works out the tariff by hand with the calculator (F-hr_transcript-3cd6fa). Lonio now owns the result (D-001), so a wrong letter means a wrong tax deduction.

acceptance_criteria.title: Married employees and registered partners get C or B
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax whose civil status is Married or Registered partnership (the calculator's 'married or registered partnership' group, D-003)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the base tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is C if the spouse or partner works or receives replacement income, and B if not. Children never change this letter.

acceptance_criteria.title: Single, divorced, separated and widowed employees get H or A
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax whose civil status is Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated (the calculator's 'single, divorced, separated or widowed' group, D-003)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the base tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is H if at least one child counts with H (per-child result, rule child_result), otherwise A.

acceptance_criteria.title: Replacement-income and special tariffs never occur
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the base tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is always A, B, C or H. Tariffs G and Q (replacement income) and special tariffs such as D (second job) are never derived during onboarding.

stories.title: Replace the base letter with the cross-border letter where the cross-border tariff applies
stories.i_want: employees living in Germany who meet the cross-border conditions to get the cross-border tariff letter (L, M, N or P) instead of the base letter
stories.so_that: cross-border commuters are taxed at the cross-border tariff the calculator gives them, and everyone else at the normal tariff
stories.priority_reason: HR finds the cross-border cases the hardest part of the calculator ('much more complicated', F-hr_transcript-8595fb). Lonio now has to compute them itself (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border tariff replaces A, B, C, H with L, M, N, P
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Germany for whom the cross-border tariff applies (rule cross_border_tariff: daily return with a certificate of residence handed in, or no daily return, daily return reasonable and no more than 60 non-return days expected)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the final tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: base letter A becomes L, B becomes M, C becomes N and H becomes P.

acceptance_criteria.title: Otherwise the base letter is kept
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax for whom the cross-border tariff does not apply. This covers employees living in Switzerland, Liechtenstein or any other country, and Germany residents without a certificate of residence ('no' or 'not yet'), without a reasonable daily return, or expecting more than 60 non-return days.
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the final tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: the final letter is the base tariff letter (A, B, C or H).

stories.title: Compute and record the full source tax tariff code
stories.i_want: Lonio to compute the complete Zurich tariff code (final tariff letter, child digit, church-tax suffix) for every employee subject to source tax and record it for me
stories.so_that: I no longer have to sit with the answers and click through the canton's calculator for each new employee
stories.priority_reason: HR's current process is a manual walk-through of the calculator for each employee (F-hr_transcript-3cd6fa). Replacing it is an explicit product decision (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Tariff code is letter, child digit and suffix
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax who does not fall under the Liechtenstein no-liability case
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio computes the tariff code from the employee's answers
acceptance_criteria.then: the tariff code is the final tariff letter, then the child digit (the number of children that count, with or without H; 0 without children), then the church-tax suffix, for example A0N, C1Y, L0Y or N1Y. The code is recorded for HR. Paths the calculator was not explored for (residence block for A/B/H, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N) are checked against the calculator before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents with daily return or at most 45 non-return days get no tariff code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Liechtenstein who returns daily, or who does not return daily and expects at most 45 work-related non-return days
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio computes the source tax result
acceptance_criteria.then: instead of a tariff code, Lonio records 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' for HR and flags the case for HR. How HR sees the flag belongs to the later HR-side spec (D-034).

then.expect: in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees not subject to source tax get no tariff code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who is not subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax)
acceptance_criteria.then: no tariff code is computed or recorded for this employee, and none of the source tax questions were asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Tariff code always reflects the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee whose answers that feed the tariff code have changed, either before submission or later by HR (for example a marriage, a new child, or a certificate of residence handed in after a 'not yet')
acceptance_criteria.when: the tariff code is looked at
acceptance_criteria.then: it is always derived again from the latest answers. No earlier code is kept as the result. How HR changes answers after submission belongs to the later HR-side spec (D-034, D-037).
